issues.t: CUE touchscreen freezes, cracks or stops responding to touch
issues.sym: The center screen locks up, lags, ignores touches in some areas, or shows a spiderweb pattern under the glass. Radio, navigation and phone controls can be lost.
issues.why: The CUE screen's touch layer separates and cracks with heat and age, and the software is prone to freezing. Owners report this as the most common ATS complaint.
issues.next: Try a system reset by holding the power button. If the screen is cracked or dead in spots, replace the touch panel; aftermarket panels are an option instead of a dealer head unit.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out (recall)
issues.sym: A 'Service Power Steering' message appears and the steering suddenly becomes very heavy, most noticeably at low speeds and when parking.
issues.why: The electric power steering gear can lose its assist. GM recalled the 2017 ATS first and later added 2017-2018 cars in a second campaign.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the NHTSA recall lookup. If the warning appears, slow down, hold the wheel firmly and have the dealer replace the steering gear for free.

issues.t: Eight-speed automatic shudders or shifts harshly
issues.sym: A shake like driving over rumble strips at steady speeds around 25-50 mph, plus harsh or hesitant shifts.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch in the 8-speed automatic shudders. GM bulletin 18-NA-355 calls for flushing in a revised transmission fluid.
issues.next: Ask a GM dealer about bulletin 18-NA-355. A full fluid exchange usually fixes it; if not, the torque converter may need replacing.

issues.t: Turbo loses boost or fails on the 2.0T
issues.sym: Check engine light, weak acceleration, a 'reduced power' feel, or the engine shaking and not getting past about 40 mph.
issues.why: Owners report turbo inlet and turbocharger failures on the 2.0L turbo, sometimes at fairly low miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read quickly. A loose or cracked intake pipe is a simple fix; a failed turbo needs replacing.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic shifts harshly or the torque converter fails
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, shudder, or slipping. A few owners also had transmission cooler lines leaking fluid.
issues.why: Owners report torque converter and valve body failures and leaking cooler lines on the 6-speed automatic.
issues.next: Check the fluid for leaks and get a scan for transmission codes. Catching a cooler line leak early avoids burning up the transmission.

issues.t: Rear differential and axle seals leak
issues.sym: Oily spots under the rear of the car, a gear-oil smell, or a whine or hum from the rear on the highway if fluid runs low.
issues.why: Seals on the rear differential and axle shafts wear and seep. Some cars also needed axle bearing or full differential replacement.
issues.next: Have the rear differential fluid level checked. Replacing a leaking seal can prevent having to replace a differential that ran dry.

issues.t: Oil leak from the front timing cover on the V6
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the engine and a burning oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The sealant around the engine front (timing) cover on the 3.6L V6 lets oil seep out over time.
issues.next: Watch the oil level. The cover must be removed and resealed, which is a large labor job.

issues.t: Driver front airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing until a crash. In a deployment the inflator can burst and throw metal pieces at the driver.
issues.why: The driver-side front airbag inflator on some 2015-2016 cars can rupture when it fires. GM recalled them in 2026.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and book the free driver airbag module replacement as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Shift cable can detach (car may roll away) (recall)
issues.sym: The gear shown on the dash may not match where the shifter is. The car can roll after you put it in Park and turn it off.
issues.why: The shift cable can come off its mount on the transmission, so the lever no longer moves the transmission.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the free recall inspection is done. Have the dealer check and reseat the cable.

issues.t: Brake pedal bracket can break (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal may feel loose or suddenly travel further, and braking power can drop.
issues.why: A bracket linking the brake pedal to the pushrod that works the brakes can crack and break.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Get the free dealer inspection and bracket replacement right away. Stop driving if the pedal feels abnormal.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can come loose and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell under the hood, a check engine light, or a rough-running engine.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump on the engine can separate from its mount and damage the fuel line, which can leak fuel near hot engine parts.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel. The dealer replaces the pump and fuel pipe for free under the recall.

issues.t: Rear defogger antenna module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or heat near the rear window, often while the rear defogger is running.
issues.why: The coil antenna module tied to the rear defogger can overheat, which creates a fire risk. The fix removes the automatic defogger turn-on feature.
issues.next: Check for open recalls. The dealer updates the climate control software for free.

issues.t: Sunroof switch can be bumped and close the roof (recall)
issues.sym: The sunroof starts closing when someone brushes the overhead switch, which could pinch a hand or arm.
issues.why: The sunroof switches sit flush and are easy to press by accident, which does not meet the federal power-window rule.
issues.next: The dealer installs a new switch trim plate for free. Keep kids' hands clear of the roof opening until then.

issues.t: Front seat may shift in a crash from weak weld (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can feel day to day.
issues.why: A weld on the front seat hook bracket may be incomplete, so the seat could move in a crash.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the seat weld for free. The lower seat track is replaced if needed.

issues.t: Front lap belt pretensioners may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash the lap belt could let out more than it should.
issues.why: The cable in the front lap belt pretensioner may not stay locked after it fires.
issues.next: Check that the free pretensioner replacement was done on your car.

issues.t: Brake lights flash and cruise control drops out (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights blink without your foot on the pedal, and cruise control may switch off on its own.
issues.why: A programming fault in the body control module controls the brake lights incorrectly.
issues.next: The dealer reprograms the body control module for free.

issues.t: Engine vibration and rough idle from worn engine mounts
issues.sym: The car shakes at idle or at stoplights, and the vibration can be felt in the steering wheel and seats.
issues.why: The engine mounts lose their damping. GM issued a bulletin, and many cars got new mounts.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected; a dealer can check whether the bulletin applies.

issues.t: Knocking from the steering shaft when turning
issues.sym: A clunk or knock felt in the steering wheel when turning, especially on cold mornings.
issues.why: The lower steering intermediate shaft develops play. Dealers replaced it under warranty on some cars.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect the steering shaft and front end. It is not usually an emergency, but get it checked.

issues.t: Front suspension clunks over bumps
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the front over bumps, rough pavement or driveways.
issues.why: Owners report worn front lower control arms, loose strut nuts and a worn steering knuckle causing the noise.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked; a loose part should be fixed before it wears others.

issues.t: Radiator or cooling fan failure causes overheating
issues.sym: Coolant drips, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge rising in traffic, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: Owners report radiators cracking at the seams, a leaking surge tank hose and an intermittent radiator fan on both 4-cylinder and V6 cars.
issues.next: Do not keep driving if the gauge climbs. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat sensor
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, or the passenger airbag status shows wrong. Some owners say it comes on when a phone charges on the passenger seat.
issues.why: The passenger seat occupant sensor can misread or fail, which makes the airbag system set a fault.
issues.next: Remove items from the passenger seat and see if the light clears. If it stays on, have the airbag codes read; the sensor may need replacing.

issues.t: A/C smells musty
issues.sym: A damp, moldy smell from the vents when the A/C first turns on.
issues.why: Moisture left on the A/C evaporator grows mold. Dealers treated the evaporator and added an after-blow module that dries it after shutoff.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter and have the evaporator cleaned. Running the fan with A/C off for a minute before parking also helps.

issues.t: One side blows the wrong temperature
issues.sym: One side of the cabin gets only cold air or doesn't match the setting, or the climate control acts erratic.
issues.why: A blend (mix) door or its actuator inside the dash fails, so it can't mix hot and cold air.
issues.next: Have the HVAC system scanned. Some doors need dashboard removal, so ask for a quote first.

issues.t: Check engine light from evaporative vent valve
issues.sym: Check engine light, often with code P0449. You may have trouble filling the tank.
issues.why: The evaporative emissions vent solenoid or its wiring fails.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed. The vent valve is a fairly simple part to replace.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensors fail
issues.sym: The tire pressure light stays on or a tire shows no reading even though pressures are fine.
issues.why: The battery inside a tire pressure sensor dies or the sensor fails.
issues.next: Check the tires with a gauge first. A shop can find which sensor is dead and replace it.

issues.t: Engine stalls at stops or loses power
issues.sym: The engine dies at a stoplight and restarts after a few minutes, or the car loses power and may stay in a low gear.
issues.why: Owners report stalling and power loss, but no single cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Note any warning lights and have codes read right after it happens. Have the battery and connections tested too.
